newsitem.title: UK: Nottingham holds key to UK interest rates -BOE.
newsitem.headline: Nottingham holds key to UK interest rates -BOE.

text.p: The city of Nottingham in the English Midlands -- home town of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke -- holds the key to official UK interest rates, according to Bank of England deputy governor Howard Davies.
In a tongue-in-cheek speech prepared for delivery on Friday evening in Darlington, Davies said:
"With this particular Chancellor, one thing is clear. If you want to persuade him to change rates, you need to have your finger on the pulse of economic conditions in Nottingham."

Many economists in the City of London believe the Conservative Chancellor is unduly influenced by the needs of industry in the country's industrial heartland, even though manufacturing now accounts for less than a quarter of GDP.

In a remarkably humorous address by the dry standards of the Bank of England, Davies said the central bank was extending its network of regional agents who monitor local economic developments on its behalf, adding a new office in Nottingham.
"Nottingham is, of course, the only logical choice in purely economic terms," he added.
Davies, a former director-general of the Confederation of British Industry, discoursed seriously on the importance of regional economic disparities for monetary policy.
But in one of several asides, he remarked: "At the Bank we find it difficult enough to forecast next month's RPI (a number of our economists and our press officer asked me to remove that sentence)."
In his opening remarks, Davies vigorously caricatured cliches about Britain's north-south divide, before dismissing them as tiresome and unimaginative and adding:
"I propose to abandon these cliches for the evening and I hope that any dour, curmudgeonly, mean-spirited Yorkshiremen who happen to have strayed in will be prepared to do the same."
